methodology_note: Each county's area is a cluster of hexagonal cells, sized by its total ACS population (not land area, and never touched by the week's change) and grown outward from its own real geographic location -- a discrete, grid-based cartogram, not a circle-packing one, chosen specifically to keep real neighbors adjacent and real regional shapes (the Great Lakes, Florida's peninsula) recognizable. Position and size are both fixed; only color and height (stage 3) vary by the week selected above, read from the same weekly hotspot-change data as the main map's own hotspot layer. Stage 1 shows each county's own true shape; stage 2 fades into its hex-cell cartogram shape; stage 3 raises or lowers every hex cell by that week's own change.
